The Government wants to emphasize that those being brought to Liberia are not criminals and are not being prosecuted in any manner under United States or Liberian law. They are being received as guests of the Republic of Liberia in keeping with Liberia's long-standing tradition of being a country that has provided shelter to all those seeking refuge and protection from persecution, wars and other forms of conflict. The persons to be transferred from the United States of America to Liberia should therefore be accorded full Liberian hospitality whilst in Liberia, and shall remain free to depart the country when they so desire. However, any person being brought to Liberia, who desires to make Liberia their home, will be accorded the opportunity to apply for asylum in keeping with Liberian laws. The Government of Liberia intends to provide the transferred persons with the necessary support to seek protection in Liberia and to be safe during their stay here.
The transfer of persons to Liberia is not a transaction with a quid pro quo. Liberia has not demanded or received any compensation or promise of reward in exchange for its consent to participate in the program. Liberia will receive support to help manage the program and strengthen its migration system more broadly. Liberia's gesture is entirely humanitarian and in keeping with the country's longstanding traditions.
Liberia, the first black African independent nation on the African continent has a long history of accepting people seeking refuge from political and other crises. As a matter of fact, Liberia itself was founded as a refuge for freed people of color - some of the formerly enslaved - from the United States of America and other parts of the world. The name Liberia comes from the Latin word liber, meaning "free," so Liberia means "land of the free." The country has maintained this tradition through the years. When Liberia stood as the only independent country in Africa during the period of European colonialism and domination, the country provided a safe haven for African freedom fighters in the struggles to liberate the rest of Africa, including Nelson Mandela who lived in Congo Town. Stateless African freedom fighters used Liberia as their residence and traveled the world with Liberian passports. Liberia has no history of deporting anyone for living in Liberia irregularly or without documentation.
In this case where Liberia has agreed to receive persons transferred from the United States, our decision to accept them is in keeping with existing Liberian tradition. As a country, we have always welcomed people who cannot return to their home of origin, and to reject these third country nationals would be acting against our best interest. Liberia sees this arrangement as an opportunity to showcase Liberian hospitality and goodwill towards all and we intend to maintain the tradition.
The Government of Liberia calls on our citizens and residents to treat those being transferred to Liberia with due courtesy and to accord them our true African hospitality.

title: Mehr als 300 Migranten von Holzboot vor Mauretanien gerettet
content:
Manövrierunfähiges Holzboot Mehr als 300 Migranten vor Mauretanien gerettet
Vor der Küste Mauretaniens hat die Küstenwache mehr als 300 Menschen von einem manövrierunfähigen Holzboot gerettet. Sie waren wohl auf dem Weg zu den Kanarischen Inseln - eine Route, die immer gefährlicher wird.
Die mauretanische Küstenwache hat nach eigenen Angaben mehr als 300 Migranten von einem Boot auf dem Weg nach Europa gerettet. Darunter seien 40 Kinder und Jugendliche gewesen.
Bei ihrer Rettung seien die Menschen in einer "schwierigen humanitären Lage" gewesen, teilte die Küstenwache mit. Sie hätten sich auf einem Holzboot befunden. Dieses trieb zum Zeitpunkt der Rettung in der Nacht zum Donnerstag manövrierunfähig auf dem Meer, wie die Nachrichtenagentur AFP von einem Mitarbeiter der Küstenwache erfuhr. An Bord befanden sich demnach 315 Menschen aus den westafrikanischen Ländern Gambia und Senegal.
Neue Grenzkontrollen - längere Wege auf See
In den vergangenen Monaten war es immer wieder zu schweren Unglücken vor der mauretanischen Küste gekommen, bei denen Menschen aus Westafrika versucht hatten, mit Booten die zu Spanien gehörenden Kanarischen Inseln zu erreichen. Allein im Juli seien 144 Menschen gestorben oder vermisst worden, so das Flüchtlingshilfswerk der Vereinten Nationen, UNHCR.
Eine kürzlich erfolgte Verschärfung der Seegrenzkontrollen im Senegal, in Mauretanien und Marokko führte zuletzt zu einer Verlagerung der Abfahrtsorte: Statt von Mauretanien aus stechen viele der Boote nun weiter südlich in See, insbesondere von den Küsten Gambias und Guineas. Für die Insassen verlängert dies die Zeit auf See verlängert und erhöht die Gefahren.

title: Gemeinsame Schulungen entlasten Betriebe im Waldviertel
content: Die Suche nach einem Job kann für jeden und jede herausfordernd sein. Wer jedoch eine höhere Ausbildung abschließt, hat es laut dem AMS NÖ später leichter, wieder in Beschäftigung zu kommen. „Qualifizierung ist der beste Schutz vor Arbeitslosigkeit“, so die Organisation.Um gleichzeitig die innerbetriebliche Kompetenz zu stärken und Fachkräfte zu fördern, haben sich in den letzten 26 Jahren mehr als 50 Unternehmen im Waldviertel in einem Qualifizierungsverbund zusammengeschlossen. Die Betriebe planen Schulungen zusammen und würden so Kosten sparen, auf Förderungen zugreifen sowie voneinander lernen können, heißt es aus dem AMS.800 Personen geschultIm Vorjahr haben knapp 800 Mitarbeitende entsprechende Weiterbildungen im Verbund absolviert – einige von ihnen in der Firma GLS Tanks, die im Bezirk Gmünd emaillierte Stahlbehälter und Silos herstellt. Personalchefin Katharina Sagaster sieht in dem Bündnis eine Möglichkeit, „Schulungen direkt in der Region anzubieten und den organisatorischen Aufwand deutlich zu reduzieren“.Um einen Qualifizierungsverbund zu gründen, braucht es laut dem AMS mindestens drei Unternehmen. Die Hälfte der Mitglieder müssen Klein- und Mittelbetriebe sein. Seitens des AMS werden eine externe Beratung sowie Weiterbildungskosten für bestimmte Zielgruppen gefördert. title: Towards the implementation of cannabis-focused apps in early intervention services for psychosis: A qualitative investigation of patient and clinician perspectives.
content: Cannabis use is highly prevalent among young adults with first-episode psychosis (FEP) and is associated with poorer clinical and functional outcomes. Mobile health interventions may help address structural barriers to delivering cannabis-focused psychosocial interventions within early intervention services (EIS), yet little is known about how such tools are experienced and integrated into routine care. This study explored young adults with FEP and clinician experiences of two cannabis-focused mobile interventions, iCanChange (iCC) and Cannabis Harm-reducing App to Manage Practices Safely (CHAMPS), with a particular focus on implementation within EIS. Qualitative exploratory study using semi-structured individual interviews. Data were analysed using a reflexive thematic approach informed by the integrated Promoting Action on Research Implementation in Health Services (i-PARIHS) framework. Six EIS programs in Canada (five in Quebec and one in Nova Scotia). Twenty-eight young adults aged 18-35 years with FEP who participated in the intervention arms of the iCC or CHAMPS pilot randomized controlled trials, and 17 EIS clinicians from multiple professional backgrounds. Semi-structured interviews explored experiences of app use, perceived benefits and challenges, contextual influences, clinician involvement and factors affecting engagement and integration within EIS. Themes were mapped to the i-PARIHS domains of innovation, recipients, context and facilitation. Participants generally perceived both mobile interventions as acceptable, relevant and well aligned with the daily realities of young adults with FEP. The apps' accessibility, flexibility and non-judgmental approach supported self-reflection, autonomy and increased awareness of cannabis use. However, engagement was shaped by individual motivation, psychosis-related symptoms, competing life and treatment priorities and, for some, app-related challenges, including content-related concerns and technical issues that interfered with use. Clinician involvement was widely viewed as beneficial for sustaining engagement and supporting reflection, yet was inconsistently implemented due to time constraints, limited familiarity with app content and uncertainty regarding clinicians' roles. Cannabis-focused mobile interventions appear to be acceptable and relevant complements to standard early intervention service care for psychosis. Their successful implementation depends not only on usability, but also on active facilitation, clear clinician role definitions and adaptive integration strategies that align with real-world constraints within early intervention services.

title: Refugee passes GCSEs after fleeing war-torn Sudan
content:
Refugee passes GCSE after fleeing war-torn Sudan
- Published
A refugee who fled a war-torn country and found safety in the UK before becoming a football referee says he has proved "you can achieve your goals" after passing his GCSEs.
Nasser Hamid grew-up in a "tiny" village in Sudan, where millions have been displaced since the country's civil war began in 2023.
The 20-year-old, who was 16 at the time and could not speak English, fled his home and moved to Ipswich, where he was helped by Suffolk Refugee Support.
After passing GCSE English earlier this year, he has now achieved grade 4 in maths and said it was "one of the proudest moments in my life".
When Hamid arrived in the UK, he stayed in accommodation provided by YMCA Suffolk along with other people who only spoke Arabic.
He requested to be moved to a different shared housing block, with people who could help him learn English, and he also worked at Portman Road as a cashier.
More stories from Suffolk:
Hamid, whose mother and younger brothers remain in Sudan, said it was important to "just believe in yourself".
"With discipline and hard work, you can achieve your goals," he added.
"Thanks to Suffolk New College, without their help I wouldn't be standing here."
An injury ended his dreams of becoming a footballer and he has qualified as a referee with the help of the Ipswich Town Foundation.
He has overseen a charity game at Portman Road and officiated Saturday and Sunday league matches.
"I went to the Edinburgh International Cup and I'd like to continue to progress – to the Championship, the Premier League, and the World Cup, who knows," he said.
Hamid now wants to become an engineer.
David Squire, head of maths at Suffolk New College and Hamid's teacher, said: "I've never been prouder of a learner in my life."

title: Will personalised mRNA vaccines transform cancer treatments?
content:
Every cancer is different. Because of that, researchers have for decades been working on personalised cancer vaccines designed to make the immune system recognise and attack cancers specific to each individual. The results have been mixed, but now a personalised cancer vaccine has produced positive results in a final-stage trial for the first time.
Moderna announced on 19 August that people who had undergone surgery to remove severe skin cancers, called melanomas, survived longer without the cancer returning or spreading to other parts of the body if they were given a personalised mRNA cancer vaccine in conjunction with another immunotherapy, compared with receiving that immunotherapy alone.
The hope is that this personalised vaccine will work for many other types of cancer. Trials are already underway for certain kinds of lung, kidney and bladder forms of the condition. The other big mRNA company, BioNTech, is also testing personalised cancer vaccines in human trials.
Advertisement
What is a cancer vaccine?
Cancers are caused by cells accumulating mutations to the point where they go rogue and start multiplying out of control. Mutations in proteins that protrude from the surface of cells also make cancer cells “look” a bit different to other cells. This allows our immune system to recognise and kill off many cancers without us ever knowing about it. But some cancers slip through the net – the idea of cancer vaccines is to teach the immune system to recognise them.
How are these vaccines made?
In the case of the Moderna vaccine, called intismeran autogene, a sample of a person’s cancer – a biopsy – is sequenced. It is then compared with their healthy blood cells to identify surface proteins on the cancerous cells that have distinctive mutations. Up to 34 are selected, and mRNAs coding for those proteins are made and put in the vaccine.
What happens next?
The cancer vaccine is injected into muscles, just like with the covid-19 mRNA vaccine. Cells in the muscles then temporarily produce the cancer proteins, triggering an immune response to them.
Why use mRNA vaccine technology?
It is possible to use other kinds of vaccines, but mRNA has two huge advantages: speed and cost. Making protein-based vaccines requires using living cells, which is time-consuming and requires many safety checks. For people with cancer, the faster a vaccine can be created, the better.
What immunotherapy was the vaccine combined with for the trial?
It is a so-called anti-PD-1 therapy consisting of an antibody called pembrolizumab (Keytruda). Many cancers evolve to evade immune attack by putting up a “don’t attack me” sign. Immune cells “read” this sign with the help of a protein on their surface called PD-1.
Blocking PD-1 makes the “don’t attack me” sign invisible to immune cells, so they attack regardless. However, anti-PD-1 treatments work only if the immune system is already trying to attack a cancer, hence the advantage of combining them with a cancer vaccine to provoke that attack.
How well did the combined treatment work?
Moderna hasn’t told us yet. The company has announced only that the results of the phase III trial “demonstrate statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements” in survival times.
The trial involved 1137 people who, after surgery to remove melanomas, were randomly assigned to get both the vaccine and pembrolizumab, or just pembrolizumab. What we do know is that in an earlier trial involving 157 people with melanoma over five years, the combination of the vaccine and pembrolizumab cut the risk of recurrence by 50 per cent and the risk of spread to other parts of the body by 60 per cent, compared with pembrolizumab alone.
When will this treatment become available?
Analysts speaking to the Financial Times say it could be approved next year. But because it is an individualised treatment, scaling up production will be much more complex than with a standard vaccine.
It also isn’t clear yet what the pricing will be – even with the help of mRNA technology, it won’t be cheap. A January report by Reuters suggested it would cost around $200,000 per treatment. No wonder Moderna’s share price is soaring.
Will this work for all cancers?
The hope is it will work for many cancers, but we will have to wait on more phase III trial results to be sure. That said, several other earlier-stage mRNA cancer vaccine trials have produced promising results. In fact, a study last year estimated that on the basis of these results, their potential health benefits could be worth around $75 billion a year in the US alone.
Are there any approved cancer vaccines already?
Not like intismeran autogene. Some sources will tell you there are three approved vaccines for treating cancer: Provenge, BCG and T-VEC.
But Provenge is a treatment that involves removing immune cells from a person’s body, exposing them to a prostate cancer protein, then replacing them. BCG is the tuberculosis vaccine, which just happens to help treat some bladder cancers for reasons we still don’t understand. And T-VEC is a live herpes simplex virus engineered to kill cancer cells.
So only one of the three is a conventional vaccine, and its anti-cancer action is completely incidental.
What about the HPV and hepatitis vaccines?
These vaccines prevent infections by viruses that can cause cancers, rather than targeting cancers directly, which is an even better approach. The HPV vaccine has proved incredibly effective at preventing cervical cancer, for instance.

title: Aardappeldemo’s bieden telers nieuwe inzichten
content:
Aardappeldemo’s bieden telers nieuwe inzichten
Proefboerderij Wijnandsrade opende op donderdag 13 augustus haar deuren voor een veldbijeenkomst in het kader van lopende aardappeldemo’s. Centraal stond een toekomstgerichte teelt, met een emissiereductie van nitraat en gewasbeschermingsmiddelen naar het grondwater. Ook was er aandacht voor een weerbare teelt.
De akkerbouw staat onder druk door uitdagingen als aangescherpte regelgeving en extreem weer. ‘Bij een temperatuur van boven de 25 graden Celsius doet een aardappel helemaal niets meer’, vertelt LLTB-projectleider Guido Schriever. Een transitie naar andere teeltmethodes met robuustere rassen is dus essentieel. ‘Het is een reëel en noodzakelijk verhaal om de toekomst van de akkerbouw in Limburg veilig te stellen.’
Vanuit het project WaterWinst werd eerder dit jaar een demonstratieveld aangelegd met vijf robuustere aardappelrassen. Ook werd vanuit Propositie Heuvelland en Delphy onderzoek gestart naar biostimulanten, stikstofefficiëntie en PFAS-vrije aardappelteelt. In juli konden geïnteresseerden al een eerste indruk krijgen van het verloop van de proeven.
Tijdens de veldbijeenkomst was er aandacht voor de ontwikkelingen van een viertal proeven uitgevoerd op de demovelden. Binnen WaterWinst ging het om twee van deze demo’s. Voor de eerste demo werd in samenwerking met 3 Point Potatoes gekeken naar nieuwe robuuste rassen, geteeld met een laag stikstofniveau en zonder beregening.
Verschillende stikstofniveaus
De andere demo, in samenwerking met Wageningen University & Research (WUR), ging over vier nieuwe aardappelrassen, met twee verschillende stikstofniveaus en zonder beregening. Daarnaast nam Propositie Heuvelland samen met WUR het voortouw met een proef over worteldominant telen met behulp van biostimulanten.
Delphy nam deel met een demo uitgevoerd met biostimulanten en PFAS-vrije middelen. De proeven worden gerealiseerd in samenwerking met Deltaplan Agrarisch Waterbeheer (DAW). De resultaten lijken veelbelovend. ‘We zien nieuwe rassen in zo’n droog, heet jaar beter presteren dan oude rassen’, stelt Schriever.
Lees ook: Nieuwe koers voor aardappelteelt op Zuid-Limburgse lössgrond
In groepjes gingen de deelnemers op pad om de demo’s te bekijken. Omdat de demovelden niet op dezelfde locatie liggen, gingen de bezoekers per huifkar naar de percelen toe. Aan het begin van de avond konden bezoekers genieten van verse frites van het nieuwe ras Donata, beschikbaar gesteld door 3 Point Potatoes. Met een gevulde buik kon iedereen vervolgens meeluisteren naar drie lezingen.
Met een grote opkomst van circa tachtig mensen was de veldbijeenkomst op Proefboerderij Wijnandsrade een groot succes. Naast de Nederlandse boeren was er ook belangstelling vanuit Duitsland en België. Daarbij waren ook de ketenpartijen goed aangesloten. Tijdens het bezoek werd er onder de bezoekers flink gediscussieerd over robuuste teelt. Met temperaturen tot 38 graden voerden de uitdagingen voor aardappelteelt onder extreme weersomstandigheden de boventoon.

title: The question on bike lanes shouldn’t be about constitutional rights but if they save lives
content:
Sometimes you just have to let the stupid sink in. It’s the only way to cope. The stupidity is so strong and overwhelming you must surrender. You must let it soak you, the way you would if you were caught, without an umbrella, in a sudden August rainstorm.
Such has been the case with the “Great Bike Lane Constitutional Debate of 2026.” It’s a tale of histrionics and misdirection.
Our story begins in November 2024, when Doug Ford’s Conservatives passed the “Reducing Gridlock, Saving You Time Act.” The legislation forced local governments to seek provincial approval to install new bike lanes (if it meant removing an existing car lane) and allowed the provincial government to remove bike lanes.
As we all can see, the 2024 “Reducing Gridlock, Saving You Time Act” has been a rousing success. Traffic moves smoothly. Gridlock no longer exists. Traffic accidents and fatalities are at an all-time minimum. Mission accomplished.
But not everybody back then could see what magic lay on the horizon. Cycle Toronto, a bike advocacy group, filed a human rights complaint, trying to block the demolition of 19 kilometres of bike lanes along Bloor Street, Yonge Street and University Avenue in Toronto. It argued the “lane removal plan was an unconstitutional safety risk.” In 2025, Superior Court Justice Paul Schabas agreed, maintaining that it would violate their charter rights.
This caused politicos and pundits to lose their minds and Canadians were subjected to outraged articles in which outraged columnists expressed their outrage and displayed their admirable common sense.
But faster than you can snatch a bottle of American bourbon from the shelf, the decision was made null.
On July 30, three Ontario Court of Appeal judges overturned the ruling. “Removing bicycle lanes is in no way analogous to imposing a sentence of life imprisonment for spitting on the sidewalk or exposing citizens to a high risk of being murdered to prevent nuisances,” wrote Justice Grant Huscroft. “It is mere traffic regulation and cannot be described as ‘draconian.’”
This was the cue for bike lane advocates to write outraged columns expressing their outraged outrage.
All this angst and anger over the question of whether or not bike lanes are a human right.
They aren’t.
But they do prevent cyclists from dying. The avalanche of research is pretty much unassailable.
A study from the University of Colorado Denver found that “bicycling infrastructure – specifically, separated and protected bike lanes – leads to fewer fatalities and better road-safety outcomes for all road users.”
The U.S. Federal Highway Administration has stated that bicycle lanes can reduce between 30 to 49 per cent of crashes on urban local roads (FHWA, 2022).
The joint study of temporary “pop-up” bike lanes in New Jersey found that bike lanes lessened the occurrence of “Right-hook turns (where a motor-vehicle turns right while a cyclist continues straight) which have been found to be particularly more hazardous for cyclists than other crash typologies.”
This is important, because a 2018 study from the University of Toronto, which studied the eye movements of drivers at busy Toronto intersections “found that more than half failed to make necessary scans for pedestrians or cyclists at right turns.”
Don’t bike? Well, you may benefit as well. Bike lanes have also been shown to lower the risk of pedestrian injuries and fatalities.
The question is not “Are bike lanes a right guaranteed by the Charter of Rights and Freedoms?” It’s “Do they save lives?”
If your position is: “I am comfortable with people dying if that will improve the flow of traffic,” then say that. Don’t trip out over it being a constitutional right.
I mean, that’s where we are collectively as a society anyhow. Every day you see news of more people killed in or by cars. If guns were doing the killing, we’d all be (pardon me) up in arms, but we accept traffic deaths as the cost of doing business.
As for cycling advocates who believe that bike lanes not only make people safer but can cure most illnesses and will usher in a new two-wheeled Utopia, your vehement unwillingness to accept that every road does not need a bike lane weakens an otherwise strong argument.
The bike lanes on Bloor Street should be renamed “E-bike Alley.” They achieve little and there are are close east-west alternatives through the middle of the city on Harbord Street and Wellesley Street. The Bloor lanes should be removed.
In Canadian cities, many bike lanes sit empty during the winter months, and these bike lane ghost towns can be frustrating to see when you are stuck in gridlock.
So much of the discourse around bike lanes is anchored in whether we “like” bicyclists or whether drivers are all fascists. This should have no bearing on the discussion. I dislike virtually everyone, but I don’t want them all to die or get injured.
“Liking” a particular group should not be the litmus test on whether or not you care if they get hurt. You should care because they are fellow human beings. Children all know this instinctively but somehow we unlearn it as we age.
The bike lane to hell is paved with pointless bickering.

title: Keta Municipal Hospital marks 100 years of continuous healthcare service
content:
Audio By Carbonatix
Keta Municipal Hospital in the Volta Region is set to mark 100 years of continuous healthcare service to residents of Keta and surrounding communities.
The Ghana Health Service facility, located in the Keta Municipality, will celebrate its centenary in October 2026, marking a century of service to the people and a significant milestone in the history of healthcare delivery in the area.
The anniversary is expected to provide an opportunity to reflect on the hospital’s contribution to healthcare over the past century, while highlighting its current capabilities, challenges and plans for the future.
The centenary activities, which began in July, will run through October and are expected to bring together healthcare professionals, stakeholders, sister health institutions, community members and other partners.
Among the activities planned are a scientific lecture, an inter-hospital fun games event, a medical screening exercise and a community clean-up exercise.
The activities will culminate in a main event week and the anniversary climax in October.
Beyond celebrating its history, the hospital intends to use the centenary to draw attention to its present-day operations and the needs required to improve healthcare delivery.
The anniversary will highlight the hospital’s service offerings, staff welfare concerns and the need for equipment retooling to enable the facility to respond effectively to the healthcare needs of the municipality and surrounding communities.
The centenary planning committee said the celebration is also intended to create greater public awareness of the hospital’s role and encourage broader engagement with stakeholders on its future direction.
The milestone comes as the hospital reflects on a century in which its role in the health needs of Keta and neighbouring communities has continued to evolve alongside Ghana’s healthcare system.
The organisers are therefore seeking to use the centenary as more than a commemoration of the past, but also as a platform to discuss how the hospital can be strengthened to meet the healthcare needs of future generations.

title: California Legislature passes balcony solar bill
content:
Next Upcoming
Rural America & The Clean Energy Transition at Climate Week NYC
By Canary Media
Californians could soon put solar panel kits on balconies and in backyards to lower their electric bills — without utility approval.
On Wednesday, state lawmakers passed the Plug and Play Solar Act (Senate Bill 868) to legalize balcony solar, a form of DIY clean energy that’s taken off in Germany. The bill, which garnered bipartisan support, now heads to the desk of Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom. His office declined to say if he’ll sign or veto it within the 30-day deadline; if he does neither, it would still become law and take effect Jan. 1, 2027.
“Imagine being able to reduce your annual electric bill by $400, which is what is estimated here, simply by plugging in one of these devices and leaving it in the sun,” state Sen. Scott Wiener (D), who wrote the bill, said at a Monday press conference on the legislation. “This is a level of convenience in terms of installation and energy savings that we have not seen before.”
Balcony solar kits, already sold by a few businesses in the U.S., put home solar in the hands of millions of renters and homeowners who can’t have panels installed on their roofs. The portable panels push power into a standard 120-volt wall outlet; that electricity then flows to the nearest power-hungry devices, such as the fridge, computer, Wi-Fi router, lights, and air conditioner.
If enacted, California’s legislation would allow households to install plug-in solar systems sized up to 1,200 watts per residence without the costly and potentially time-consuming utility interconnection process that’s required for larger rooftop arrays. Even a 400-watt system can cover roughly 14% of an apartment’s energy use, according to the Environmental Working Group, a nonprofit that advocated for the bill.
The Golden State’s embrace of balcony solar follows a tsunami of support nationwide. More than half of states have considered plug-in solar legislation in the last year, and so far, eight have adopted balcony solar laws: Colorado, Connecticut, Maine, Maryland, New Hampshire, Utah, Vermont, and Virginia. New York passed a bill in June, but boosters are still on tenterhooks as to whether Gov. Kathy Hochul (D) will sign it.
“California is going to have a huge impact on this market,” said Cora Stryker, co-founder of plug-in solar nonprofit Bright Saver. The state’s economy is the largest and among the fastest growing in the nation. “Manufacturers are going to see this and seize upon the opportunity.”
The bad news: Households won’t be able to get plug-in solar that meets the bill’s requirements right away. The state would allow only balcony solar kits that have been certified safe to use by a nationally recognized testing laboratory. One of these organizations, safety company UL Solutions, began testing plug-in systems this year under its new standard, UL 3700, but no product has yet earned certification.
The rule is more restrictive than those adopted by some other states. For example, Utah and Maryland require that the individual kit components pass safety standards, rather than the entire system, according to Stryker.
Stryker said she’s worried that California’s stringent approach could put a damper on balcony solar’s growth in the state in the near term, especially for renters. In its current form, the UL 3700 standard still requires an electrician to get involved, the opposite of plug and play. Still, Bernadette Del Chiaro, the Environmental Working Group’s senior vice president for California, said she expects the standard to evolve to include DIY systems as soon as next year.
Another wrinkle: The legislation includes an expiration date, which the state’s largest utility, Pacific Gas and Electric, appears to have lobbied for. On Jan. 1, 2030, Californians will no longer be able to install plug-in solar without first getting their utility’s sign off.
“We would expect the Legislature to reconsider that sunset in 2028 and at the latest 2029,” Del Chiaro said.
Wiener believes, despite its challenges, the plug-in solar bill will be transformative for Californians. “Balcony solar is incredibly important,” Wiener told Canary Media. “This is a way to lower people’s cost of living when people need relief. … I’m glad that we’re finally making it happen.”

title: Govt lifts livestock market restrictions in four districts
content: The government has reopened livestock markets in four Eastern Province districts following a decline in the Rift Valley fever (RVF) outbreak, allowing farmers and traders to resume the sale and movement of cattle, goats and sheep. The reopened markets are in Nyagatare, Gatsibo, Ngoma and Kirehe, according to a livestock market schedule for August and September 2026. We are lifting progressively, said Solange Uwituze, the Minister of State for Agriculture and Animal Resources. ALSO READ: Meat prices disrupted amid Rift Valley Fever outbreak On June 26, RAB placed livestock under quarantine in six districts following an outbreak of RVF. The restrictions were later extended to the entire Eastern Province and several districts in the Northern Province, except Gakenke. As part of measures to contain the disease, livestock in affected areas were quarantined, while slaughtering and meat sales were prohibited. Agriculture and Animal Resources Minister Telesphore Ndabamenye recently said livestock had been vaccinated and that the supply of animals to meat markets could resume soon. However, livestock markets in Bugesera, Rwamagana and Kayonza, as well as those in the Northern Province, have not yet been reopened. The schedule lists 12 market days across the four districts between August 21 and September 28. Nyagatare has the busiest schedule, with six market days across four locations. The Katabagemu market will be held on August 21 and September 18, while Rwimiyaga will operate on August 28 and September 28. Tabagwe and Karangazi markets will be held on September 4 and September 11, respectively. ALSO READ: Rwanda tackles RVF using ‘One Health’ approach Kirehe will have two market days at Nyarubuye, on August 24 and September 14. Ngoma will also have two market days at the Gituku/Rukira market, on August 31 and September 21. Gatsibo will hold markets at Rwimbogo on September 7 and Kabarore on September 25. A letter signed by Eastern Province Governor Pudence Rubingisa on August 19 said the schedule followed a decline in the RVF outbreak in the four districts. It noted that the schedule could be changed if necessary and would be replaced with another one after September 28. Authorities have also imposed measures to ensure livestock sold at the reopened markets can be traced. In Ngoma, for instance, farmers have been instructed not to bring cattle to the market without ear tags, while traders have been told to buy only cattle that have entered the market enclosure and bear ear tags. The reopening has brought relief to traders who had been hit by the restrictions. George Gatarayiha, a cattle trader in the Eastern Province, said he previously bought between 20 and 30 cows a week for supply to abattoirs in Kigali. About 10 of his cows died from RVF, causing him significant losses. ALSO READ: Eastern Province on alert as Rift Valley Fever kills over 100 cows in Ngoma District “I have also read the announcement, and as traders, we are relieved. We had been unable to work for some time, so this will help us return to business,” he said. He urged farmers and traders to comply with disease-control measures to prevent another outbreak from disrupting livestock trade.

Upravo je takva iskustva svojih klijentica tijekom rada u fitnessu primijetila Nika Ćustić, pa je odlučila napraviti prostor u kojem će se žene moći osjećati opuštenije i trenirati uz više privatnosti.
Sa samo 22 godine ostvarila je ideju na kojoj je godinama radila i 2025. otvorila privatnu teretanu namijenjenu isključivo ženama. Do vlastitog prostora nije došla preko noći - tri godine radila je oko 12 sati dnevno, šest dana u tjednu i istovremeno štedjela kako bi ostvarila svoj cilj.
S Nikom smo razgovarali o tome zašto se dio žena ne osjeća ugodno u klasičnim teretanama, kako je s 19 godina počela graditi karijeru, što joj je bilo najteže na putu do vlastitog prostora te zašto ne želi da njezin posao jednog dana preraste u mjesto na kojem je najvažnije imati što više ljudi.
Karijeru je počela graditi s 19 godina
Nika je s 19 godina završila tečaj za osobnu trenericu i počela raditi u teretanama, gdje je stekla iskustvo i prve klijentice. Kasnije je nekoliko godina s njima radila u unajmljenom prostoru, a najveći izazov na početku bio joj je, kaže, izgraditi vlastito ime.
"Kad sam počela, imala sam samo 19 godina i nisam imala iza sebe neko veliko ime ili godine iskustva. Morala sam postupno steći povjerenje klijentica i pokazati im da znam što radim", podijelila je.
U konkurenciji velikog broja trenera i teretana željela je pronaći ono po čemu će se njezin pristup razlikovati. Tijekom rada je shvatila da dijelu žena posebno znače individualan pristup, privatnost i atmosfera u kojoj se osjećaju ugodno. Uz posao je postupno širila krug klijentica i štedjela za ono što je od početka željela - vlastiti prostor.
Tri godine radila je oko 12 sati dnevno
Takav je tempo trajao tri godine. Radila je dvokratno, oko 12 sati dnevno i šest dana u tjednu, a pauza joj je najčešće bila između 12 i 14 sati. Tada bi otišla kući ručati, obavila što je trebala ili ponekad otišla na kavu s prijateljicom.
"Iskreno, bilo je teško, pogotovo kada takav tempo traje dugo. Bilo je trenutaka kada sam bila iscrpljena i kada sam se pitala koliko još mogu tako, ali nikada nisam ozbiljno razmišljala da odustanem od ideje", prisjeća se.
Motivirao ju je cilj kojem se postupno približavala. Ostvarila ga je 2025. godine, kada je s 22 godine otvorila privatnu teretanu isključivo za žene. Prostor u kojem se nalazi teretana prije je bio kafić.
Nekadašnji kafić nakon uređenja dobio je potpuno novi izgled. Nika je prostor uredila i opremila za treninge, a upravo je ondje konačno mogla ostvariti koncept o kojem je razmišljala tijekom prethodnih godina.
"Nema gužve, čekanja na sprave ni osjećaja da su sve oči uprte u tebe"
"Otvaranje vlastite teretane bilo mi je ostvarenje cilja na kojem sam godinama radila. Bila sam uzbuđena, ali sam osjećala i određenu dozu straha jer ipak je to bio velik korak za curu od 22 godine", prisjeća se.
Klijentice su, kako kaže, dobro prihvatile koncept. "Mislim da su posebno prepoznale ono što sam i sama željela postići - nema gužve, nema čekanja na sprave i nema osjećaja da su sve oči uprte u tebe."
U jednom terminu zato treniraju najviše dvije žene, što joj omogućuje da se posveti svakoj od njih. Takav pristup posebno odgovara ženama koje su ranije osjećale nelagodu pri samoj pomisli na odlazak na trening.
Klijentice su joj govorile o strahu i nesigurnosti
Dok je radila u klasičnim teretanama, Nika je primijetila da se dio žena ondje ne osjeća opušteno. Osim gužve i čekanja na sprave, smetao im je osjećaj da ih drugi promatraju, osobito ako tek počinju trenirati, ne znaju koristiti neku spravu ili nisu sigurne izvode li vježbe pravilno.
"Često mi kažu da su prije imale neku vrstu straha ili nesigurnosti kada bi trebale otići u klasičnu teretanu. Najljepše mi je kada vidim da žena koja je na početku bila jako nesigurna nakon nekog vremena samouvjereno uđe u teretanu", otkrila je.
Želi da kod nje mogu doći kako god žele, pa i u širokoj trenirci i bez šminke, bez razmišljanja o tome tko ih gleda ili osuđuje. Važna joj je i prijateljska atmosfera u kojoj se međusobno motiviraju, a čak i glazbu prilagođava ženama koje u tom trenutku treniraju.
"Fitness nije uvijek priča o mršavljenju"
Među ženama s kojima je radila posebno pamti klijenticu koja je na početku imala oko 45 kilograma, a tijekom dvije godine redovitih treninga i promjena u prehrani došla je do oko 60. Fizička transformacija pritom je bila samo jedan dio njezine priče.
Nika ističe da su klijentici komentari drugih o izgledu teško padali. Ispričala joj je kako su joj jednom na svadbi govorili da je premršava i da bi se trebala udebljati. Stoga su tijekom treninga često razgovarale i o njezinim nesigurnostima. "Tijekom dvije godine rada napravila je ogromnu fizičku promjenu, ali meni je još važnije ono što se dogodilo s njezinim samopouzdanjem", napominje.
"Ta mi je transformacija posebno važna jer pokazuje da fitness nije uvijek priča o mršavljenju. Nekad je najveća promjena upravo naučiti prihvatiti svoje tijelo, ojačati ga i prestati svoju vrijednost gledati kroz tuđe komentare", dodaje.
Ne želi izgubiti ono zbog čega je sve počelo
Nikin radni dan sada je organiziraniji, a uz nju rade još dvije trenerice. Termini su joj uglavnom popunjeni, no napominje da ni sada nema klasično radno vrijeme jer uz same treninge posao uključuje organizaciju i komunikaciju s klijenticama. Najveća je razlika u tome što sada sama raspoređuje svoje vrijeme i može više razmišljati o daljnjem razvoju posla.
Međutim, rast za nju ne znači nužno i veći broj ljudi: "Ne želim da Women’s Only Gym postane klasična velika teretana u kojoj je najvažnije imati što više ljudi. Baš suprotno, želim zadržati privatnu atmosferu i individualni pristup zbog kojeg je cijela ideja i nastala."
Ženama koje žele početi trenirati, ali ih u tome sprječavaju nesigurnost ili nelagoda, poručuje da ne trebaju čekati trenutak u kojem će se osjećati potpuno spremno. Ne moraju odmah znati koristiti svaku spravu, napraviti savršen trening niti razmišljati o tome kako izgledaju dok vježbaju.
"Najvažnije je napraviti prvi korak i pronaći mjesto i ljude uz koje se osjećaš ugodno. Nakon toga sve postaje puno lakše", zaključila je Nika.

title: Nuoret seuraavat somevaikuttajien talousvinkkejä, mutta eivät luota niihin
content:
Jos takavuosina sijoitusvinkkejä jakoivat taksikuskit, nyt niitä jakavat erilaiset sosiaalisen median vaikuttajat. Varsinkin nuoret seuraavat aktiivisesti somevaikuttajien talousneuvoja. Tämä selviää nuorten talousosaamisbarometristä, jonka Jyväskylän yliopisto toteutti yhteistyössä finanssijätti OP Pohjolan ja Helsingin yliopiston kanssa.
Somevaikuttajien antamien talousvinkkien määrä on kasvanut räjähdysmäisesti, ja nuoret seuraavat heitä ahkerasti.
– Somevaikuttajat, jotka antavat erilaisia talousvinkkejä, ovat erittäin merkittävä taloustiedon lähde. Nuoret seuraavat heitä äärimmäisen paljon, Jyväskylän yliopiston sosiologian professori Terhi-Anna Wilska kertoi Ylen Aamun haastattelussa.
Huojentavaa on kuitenkin se, että nuorten kriittisyys on säilynyt. Wilskan mukaan nuoret eivät luota kovinkaan paljon somen talousvaikuttajiin.
– Huomattavasti enemmän luotetaan omaan perheeseen, lähipiiriin, kouluun ja pankkeihin, Wilska sanoi.
Pikarikastumisneuvoja somessa
Somessa on runsaasti epärealistisia sisältöjä, jotka tähtäävät nopeaan rikastumiseen. Professorin mukaan osa sisällöistä voi olla jopa vahingollisia. Sijoitusneuvonta on luvanvaraista toimintaa, mutta somessa annettavat vinkit eivät kuulu valvonnan piiriin. Wilska vaatii tiukempaa sääntelyä nuorille kohdistettavalle markkinoinnille ja sisällöille sosiaalisessa mediassa.
– Pitäisi ehdottomasti pystyä jotenkin kontrolloimaan sitä, minkälaista sisältöä nuorille saa kohdentaa somessa ja miten lapsille ja nuorille markkinoidaan somessa, Wilska sanoi.
– Lainsäädäntökin on hiukan jäänyt jälkeen tässä, kun tekoälypohjainen kohdentaminen on kehittynyt niin nopeasti, Wilska lisäsi.
Professorin mukaan digitaalinen talousosaaminen onkin entistä tärkeämpää nykypäivänä.
– Olisi todella paljon syytä kiinnittää huomiota nimenomaan nuorten digitaaliseen talousosaamiseen, joka on entistä tärkeämpi talousosaamisen muoto, mitä tarvitaan varsinkin nyt tekoälyn aikakaudella, hän sanoi.
Some vaikuttaa nuorten ostoksiin
Nuorilta kysyttiin talousbarometrissä muun muassa korkolaskuun ja inflaation ymmärtämiseen liittyviä kysymyksiä.
Nuorten talousosaaminen on pysynyt vakaalla tasolla ja on yleisesti ottaen hyvä. Kuluttajakäyttäytymisen saralla on vielä parannettavaa.
Barometrissa kolmasosa kokee somen sisällön ohjaavan ostoksiaan. Somen vaikutus kuluttamiseen jakautuu sukupuolen mukaan: tytöistä 20 prosenttia kertoo ostaneensa hetken mielijohteesta somesta, pojista 10 prosenttia.
Somesuositukset saavat tytöt ostamaan useammin ja somen luoma varallisuuspaine koskettaa tyttöjä enemmän. 45 prosenttia kertoi, että ihailee ihmisiä, joilla on kalliit asunnot, autot ja vaatteet.
– Mitä parempi talousosaaminen nuorilla oli, niin sitä vähemmän alttiita he olivat somen ostoimpulsseille, sosiologian professori Terhi-Anna Wilska kertoi.

title: An explainable biomedical foundation model via large-scale concept-enhanced vision-language pretraining.
content: Artificial intelligence for medical imaging is required to be accurate and interpretable to clinicians. However, current multimodal biomedical foundation models often prioritize performance over explainability. Here we present ConceptCLIP, an explainable biomedical foundation model that achieves state-of-the-art diagnostic accuracy while delivering human-interpretable explanations across diverse imaging modalities. We curate MedConcept-23M, a large-scale dataset comprising 23 million biomedical image-text-concept triplets. Leveraging this dataset, we pretrain ConceptCLIP via joint image-text and region-concept alignment for precise and interpretable medical image analysis. Across a large-scale benchmark covering 78 datasets in 10 imaging modalities, ConceptCLIP demonstrates superior diagnostic performance while providing human-understandable explanations. In a clinician user study spanning three modalities, the concept-based explanations provided by ConceptCLIP help clinicians verify model predictions and identify potential errors. As an explainable biomedical foundation model, ConceptCLIP represents a critical milestone towards the widespread clinical adoption of AI, thereby advancing trustworthy AI in medicine.

title: Camel Farming Expands Across Central Asia as Climate Pressures Mount
content:
Camels are gaining renewed economic importance in Central Asia as farmers seek new markets for their milk and governments look for livestock better suited to increasingly dry conditions. In Kazakhstan, camel numbers are rising and producers are developing markets for shubat, a fermented camel milk drink, and powdered camel milk. Uzbekistan, meanwhile, has begun working with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) to develop camel husbandry in arid areas.
Kazakhstan has more than 322,000 camels, according to government figures for 2026, an increase of 2.4% from the previous year. Most are raised in the vast arid lands in the west and south of the country.
Camels are also an important part of Turkmenistan’s livestock sector. The herd numbered about 345,000 animals in 2020.
Bactrian camels have traditionally dominated Kazakhstan’s camel herd. They can withstand sharp fluctuations between extreme heat and severe cold. Over the past two decades, Kazakhstan has also seen an increase in one-humped Arvana camels, a breed of Turkmen origin known for high milk productivity.
In Turkmenistan, the Arvana is the mainstay of the industry. These camels can produce milk even when grazing on sparse desert pastures, feeding on salt-tolerant vegetation and bitter wormwood that are of little use to many other types of livestock.
Milk Brings in the Money
Milk offers camel farmers a product that can be sold throughout the year and increasingly processed into higher-value goods. A female Kazakh Bactrian camel can produce up to about 1,750 liters of milk annually, although yields vary considerably between breeds and farming systems.
The main product on the domestic market is shubat, but larger producers have also begun processing camel milk for markets far beyond the communities where it is produced.
One of the most prominent examples is Daulet-Beket LLP in the Almaty region. When a camel-milk processing plant opened there in 2021, the farm had around 5,000 camels and was producing up to five tons of shubat a day. The plant was designed to produce as much as 30 tons of powdered camel milk a month, with products being shipped to Russia and China.
Smaller farms show how strong local demand can also sustain the industry. The Suleymanov family in the Almaty region started with two camels. By the time they were profiled in 2021, their herd had grown to around 70 animals. Sixteen were being milked each day, producing 52 to 53 liters. The family said customers frequently bought their shubat before it even reached Almaty.
Camel Farming in Turkmenistan
Turkmen state media has also highlighted privately run camel farms. A 2024 report said farmer Serdarkuli Berdyliev in Ahal province kept 320 camels, including 140 females. Average milk yields were around six liters a day.
Information about private agriculture in Turkmenistan largely comes through tightly controlled state media. Camel milk production continues to feature in official coverage alongside the country’s long-established herding traditions.
Camel wool remains a marketable product, although its market is much smaller than that for milk. In Turkmenistan, it is still used to make traditional dense fabrics and long robes that provide protection from daytime heat and nighttime cold.
Why Camels Are Becoming Useful Again
The renewed interest in camels is about more than milk. Much of Central Asia is already arid or semi-arid, while water scarcity and pasture degradation are putting growing pressure on agriculture. Camels can graze on sparse, saline vegetation and make productive use of land that is poorly suited to more demanding livestock.
Such resilience is now attracting attention elsewhere in the region. In 2026, Uzbekistan and FAO launched a project to develop camel husbandry in arid areas. Uzbekistan currently has about 17,600 camels. The initiative is intended to promote the sustainable use of rangelands and improve breeding and productivity. It also seeks to support food security and climate resilience while laying the groundwork for a national camel strategy.
Camel breeding remains a small part of agriculture in Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan. Its value lies in allowing farmers to use land where raising sheep and cattle is becoming harder or more expensive.
Kazakhstan has already shown that camel milk can find customers beyond the region through powdered milk and other processed products. The industry’s future will depend on whether producers can expand those markets enough to turn an ancient form of pastoralism into a more significant modern industry as Central Asia becomes hotter and water becomes scarcer.

title: La explosión del 'Slow Travel': "Ir con pulserita no se puede asociar a la calma, si acaso a mayor control, y un viaje debe ser todo lo contrario"
content:
McDonald's no hubiera decidido, en 1986, inaugurar su primer establecimiento en Roma, posiblemente este reportaje no existiría. Si la empresa no hubiera decidido entonces que llegaba el momento de expandir su fast food por Europa, empezando por la cuna de la cocina mediterránea, seguramente Carlo Petrini, que falleció con 76 años el pasado mayo, no habría sacado adelante el movimiento Slow Food, que empezó con una cacerolada en Piazza di Spagna en la que los participantes ofrecían platos de spaghetti, penne y otras viandas para evitar la inauguración del local.
Los Big Mac siguen sirviéndose en el mismo lugar, en pleno centro histórico de la ciudad. Pero el contrapunto ejercido por Petrini permitió fundar el movimiento global Slow Food, que defiende una alimentación «buena, limpia y justa» y se opone a la vida acelerada (hoy mucho más que en 1986), a través del respeto al medio ambiente y el trato digno a los productores. A lo largo de las siguientes décadas, el fenómeno se fue trasladando a otros aspectos de la vida. La lentitud se fue colando en la moda (Slow Fashion), el urbanismo (Slow Cities) y la salud (Slow Health o Slow Medicine).Slow Living, en definitiva.
Mientras que el Slow Travel, el fenómeno de viajar más lento y de manera más consciente, tardó un poco en llegar. Por una razón muy sencilla y que todo el mundo ha notado en sus carnes: llegan las vacaciones y lo que queremos es disfrutar al máximo y a la voz de ya. La lentitud no suele entrar en los planes: prisa por buscar el vuelo, prisa por llegar al aeropuerto, al hotel, a la playa, al restaurante de moda y a la catedral más bonita del lugar. Pero la pandemia, con su nomadismo digital y las nuevas formas de entrelazar vida personal y laboral, aceleró la necesidad de plantearse viajes diferentes.
En el año de explosión de los viajes lentos, según dicen los expertos del sector como Guillermo José Barreto, que trabaja la materia turística desde hace 23 años, analizamos con distintos viajeros contemporáneos (que nos ceden algunas de sus fotografías preferidas de sus viajes predilectos) cómo desconectar de las prisas y reconectar con el entorno -sea el que sea- de una forma más consciente. Empezando, por ejemplo, por no volar.
Es el caso de Sandra Olías, una experta en contabilidad y marketing de Barcelona que, en 2018, crea la web Viajar sin volar, donde comienza a documentar sus viajes. «Tenía fobia a volar y cada viaje en avión me hacía sentir mal. No lo disfrutaba», cuenta casi una década más tarde. «No fue una decisión premeditada ni una postura ideológica sino una manera de seguir viajando sin tener que enfrentarme a algo que me generaba malestar».
Descubrió que «viajar por tierra» le devolvía algo que ni siquiera sabía que había perdido: «La calma, el control, la sensación de que el viaje empieza justo cuando sales de casa y te subes al primer tren». Después, pensó que su experiencia, «todo lo que estaba aprendiendo», podía servirle a alguien más y empezó a narrarlo en la web, hasta convertirse en un sitio de referencia para aquellos que, por distintas razones (ambientales, personales, éticas) no quieren usar el avión.
«En mi caso no hay una sola razón», apunta Olías. «Empecé por mi cuestión personal pero ahora lo hago también por una cuestión ambiental. Cuando comparas el impacto de un vuelo con el de un tren, la diferencia es enorme», señala. Y lo explica: «Por ejemplo, un Barcelona-París en avión puede emitir más de 120 kilogramos de CO por pasajero. En tren, alrededor de 11. La reducción supera el 90%. Y esto no es una excepción: a nivel europeo, el avión emite de media cinco veces más que el tren, y en trayectos cortos puede llegar a emitir hasta 38 veces más».
Olías está hablando de lo que se conoce como flygskam, que en sueco significa «vergüenza de volar», y surge como parte del activismo ambiental en el verano de 2017: el cantante sueco Staffan Lindberg publicó un artículo junto a otras personas populares del país comprometiéndose a renunciar al avión. Entre los firmantes estaba Björn Ferry, un esquiador olímpico con medalla de oro incluida que trabajaba como comentarista deportivo. Empezó a viajar miles de kilómetros en tren para cubrir las competiciones de invierno por toda Europa y viralizó el término flygskam. Luego, se sumó la activista Greta Thunberg, que viajaba en velero, y la tendencia terminó de explotar.
En España, el pionero es Román Morales García, un aventurero nacido en Tenerife en 1962 que ha documentado sus viajes lentos, al margen de la aviación comercial, en libros como Buscando el sur (Ediciones La Palma). Lo asombroso de Morales es que viaja a pie y, a veces, hasta remando. También es «muy de andar» el escritor y viajero Gabi Martínez, quizá el mayor exponente en nuestro país de lo que se conoce como liternatura: narraciones, poemas y ensayos en los que la protagonista es la naturaleza.
«Es algo tan elemental, nuestros pies...», reflexiona Martínez en una entrevista telefónica en la que cuenta sus comienzos como viajero: «Empecé con el Interrail, durmiendo en los pasillos de los trenes, pero viajar por todo el mundo y en distintas circunstancias ha conseguido traerme a mi país, a mi familia incluso. Acabé un año en la Siberia extremeña y otro en la isla de Buda, en el delta del Ebro [escribió Delta, (Seix Barral, 2023)]. Ir con pulserita no se puede asociar a la calma, si acaso a mayor control, y un viaje debe ser todo lo contrario», señala.
Martínez habla de viajar como una «sensación» que comienza por «buscar aquel destino en el que uno se sienta más integrado con el entorno como sea posible y pensar en lo que es de verdad, como el espacio natural, donde siempre eres bienvenido y que siempre sirve de aprendizaje».
Lo que no está tan claro es que todo pichichi quiera que sus vacaciones se basen en aprender. Pero lo que no se puede negar es que desde aquella cacerolada que provocó Petrini, muchos otros pensadores han insistido en que llegaba el momento de echar el freno, en la vida en general y, en concreto, también en los viajes, que son quizá el último reducto del ser humano para desplegar sus peores instintos. Seguro que ha oído la frase: «Bueno, como aquí no me conoce nadie...».
Carl Honoré, canadiense afincado en Londres, recogió el testigo de Petrini con un libro, Elogio de la lentitud (RBA), que en 2024 cumplió dos décadas. En él, definía el Slow Travel como una forma de viajar basada en la calidad y no en la cantidad. No viajar a 40 sitios en un año sino detenerse en los lugares, adentrarse en lo local. Para Honoré, esto es un «antídoto contra la hiperaceleración»: «Frenar la marcha es un superpoder que mejora la creatividad, reduce la ansiedad y nos permite vivir con más sentido».
"Viajar lento tiene que ver con la forma en que te relacionas con un lugar. No significa necesariamente moverte despacio, sino darte tiempo para observar"
Sus palabras resuenan con las de Andrea Bergareche, una mujer que comenzó a narrar sus aventuras en internet y ahora tiene una agencia de viajes especializada en mujeres que viajan solas (Nimbala, aventuras y viajes para mujeres). Por correo electrónico, relata su punto de vista: «Para mí viajar lento tiene que ver con la forma en que te relacionas con un lugar. No significa necesariamente moverte despacio o recorrer pocos kilómetros sino darte tiempo para observar, comprender y participar de la vida cotidiana del destino. Me gusta sentarme en una terraza a observar cómo se relaciona la gente, cuáles son sus costumbres o sus pequeños rituales diarios. Me gusta hablar con locales, perderme sin un rumbo concreto por los barrios o hacer algo tan sencillo como ir al supermercado y curiosear qué productos consume la gente. Creo que muchas veces viajamos mirando los lugares, pero sin llegar a habitarlos realmente. El viaje lento consiste precisamente en eso: en dejar de ser una espectadora para convertirte, aunque solo sea unos días, en una pequeña parte de ese lugar. Cuanto más tiempo pasas observando, más empiezas a entender sus códigos, sus matices y todo aquello que normalmente pasa desapercibido cuando viajamos con prisa».
Bergareche comenzó su andadura viajera online en 2015 y dice que, «durante la última década, la transformación ha sido enorme».
«Viajar se ha vuelto más accesible y más popular que nunca, pero también se ha convertido en muchos casos en un producto de consumo rápido. Las redes sociales han tenido mucho que ver en ello. Antes llegábamos a muchos lugares con menos información y más capacidad de sorpresa. Hoy a menudo viajamos con una lista de sitios que visitar, fotos que reproducir y experiencias que consumir. Vamos al destino con una expectativa muy concreta de lo que debería ocurrir, y eso deja poco espacio para que el propio lugar nos sorprenda».
Tiene la sensación de que, mayoritariamente, «el viaje consiste en coleccionar países, monumentos, restaurantes o experiencias, a menudo sin detenernos demasiado en lo que tenemos delante». Por eso, en los viajes que organiza para mujeres, «prima el asombro y el no saber qué va a pasar». En su caso, su mejor viaje fue el que hizo en autostop por Sudamérica. «Siete meses viajando sola, durmiendo gracias a Couchsurfing con un presupuesto de solo 6-8€ diarios. Lo más valioso de aquel viaje fue precisamente no tener un plan cerrado. Eso me permitía quedarme más tiempo en los lugares que me gustaban, convivir con familias locales, participar en su día a día y dejar que fueran las personas quienes me enseñaran su realidad desde dentro. Recuerdo pasar días enteros compartiendo trayectos, comidas, conversaciones y tareas cotidianas con gente que acababa de conocer. Más que visitar lugares, sentía que estaba entrando en pequeñas vidas, en sus historias, durante unos días».
Experiencias que no aparecen en guías de viaje y que suceden porque alguien decide «dejarse llevar, estar abierto, aceptar las invitaciones, las recomendaciones y las oportunidades que van apareciendo en el camino». «Ese viaje me enseñó que muchas veces lo mejor de viajar no es lo que planeas, sino precisamente aquello que nunca habrías podido planificar y que aparece cuando dejas abierta la puerta a la posibilidad».

title: Chinese ‘family bridge’ makes 200 mountain trips yearly to connect elderly with overseas children
content:
Chinese ‘family bridge’ makes 200 mountain trips yearly to connect elderly with overseas children
In 2020, China reported that 118 million elderly individuals were living alone after their children migrated for work
A man in central China has completed more than 200 trips to remote mountain villages in a year, visiting elderly parents on behalf of their children who work and live far from home or overseas.
Tian Rui, 39, from Yichang in Hubei province, is a former rural courier who now operates a small convenience store, according to Jiupai News.
Years spent delivering parcels through scattered mountain communities provided Tian with a deep understanding of the winding roads. They also unveiled a quiet reality of rural life: elderly parents ageing alone after their children left for jobs in distant cities or overseas.
Last year, Tian decided to turn that familiarity into a unique service, visiting elderly parents on behalf of absent children and becoming what he describes as a “middleman” between generations.
Clients request his assistance in buying medicine, food, and even birthday cakes, which he carries along mountain roads to their parents’ homes. His most distant client lives in Bolivia, more than 17,000km away.
Despite improved living standards, Tian noticed that rural elderly individuals often yearn for companionship more than material support.
“What they really want is to know their children are thinking of them and to have someone to talk to,” he shared with the media.

title: Semriach kämpft gegen Abschiebung
content:
Nach der gerade noch verhinderten Abschiebung am Montag ist Familie Yabas wieder da – und umringt von Freunden und Unterstützern. Schüler Arges Yabas strahlt wieder: „Hier habe ich viele Freunde. Und wir sind hier in Sicherheit“ – „Semriach ist meine Heimat“, betont sein Vater Murat Yabas.
„Wir geben nicht nur Hilfe. Wir bekommen sie auch“
„So stellt sich eine Gemeinde Integration vor. So hat es auch bei der Familie funktioniert. Es wäre für uns alle extrem schlimm, tut persönlich weh und ist traurig, wenn das nicht funktionieren würde“, so der Bürgermeister von Semriach, Gottfried Rieger. Von einem herben Verlust für die Menschen, die ihr nahe steht, spricht auch Lehrer Johannes Brandtner, sollte es wirklich zur Abschiebung der Familie kommen.
Auch Bundespräsident Van der Bellen haben die Semriacher schon um Hilfe gebeten: „Es ist eine Familie – jeder von ihnen so empathisch – wir geben nicht nur Hilfe. Wir bekommen sie auch von ihr. Jederzeit“, unterstreicht Unterstützerin Angela Puregger.
„Wir sind dankbar. Allen Semriacher Leuten“
Vor nicht ganz drei Jahren ist die kurdische Familie aus dem türkischen Grenzgebiet zu Iran und Irak geflüchtet – vor der Verfolgung der türkischen Behörden wie sie erzählen – Brüder von Maryette Yabas sind getötet worden: „Wir haben nicht gewusst wohin, nur wollten wir einen sicheren Ort. Wir sind dankbar. Allen Semriacher Leuten“, so die Mutter, die schließlich mit ihrer Familie genau hier Sicherheit gefunden hatte.
Dass die Familie nach Semriach gekommen ist, sieht auch der Bäcker Franz Pfleger im Ort als echten Glücksfall – denn Murat Yabas arbeitet schon seit zweieinhalb Jahren in seinem Betrieb: „Ich möchte ihm die Gelegenheit geben, hier weiter zu arbeiten. Wir hoffen, dass wir ihn in Semriach halten können.“
Asylzweitantrag läuft
Die Familie ist nicht nur voll integriert – der 14-jährige Sohn spielt etwa in der GAK-Fußballjugend – die Eltern haben auch beide Arbeit und sind nicht auf Sozialleistungen angewiesen. Deshalb betont Angela Puregger, „dass wir ein anderes Gesetz bräuchten; dass man schauen sollte, wie gut Menschen integriert sind – und wie notwendig wir solche Menschen brauchen!“
Ein Brief mit einem Appell den Innenminister, mehr als 100 Unterstützungserklärungen – ein Hilfegesuch an den Bundespräsidenten: Die Semriacher tun alles, damit Familie Yabas doch bleiben darf. Zurzeit läuft ein Asylzweitantrag.

title: 10代が「わたしの居場所」表現 不登校生動画甲子園2026
content:
不登校を経験した若者によるショート動画のコンテスト「不登校生動画甲子園2026」の授賞式が24日、東京都内であった。4回目となる今年のテーマは「わたしが見つけた居場所」。全国の13～19歳から42作品の応募があり、最優秀賞には埼玉県の中学2年、coco（ココ）さん（13）の動画が選ばれた。
コンテストは動画投稿サイト「TikTok（ティックトック）」などでつくる実行委員会が主催。夏休み明けは不登校が増加する傾向があり、同じ不登校経験がある子どもからのメッセージを届けようと2023年に始まった。
動画は1分以内で、フリースクールや趣味、夢などで見つけたそれぞれの「居場所」を表現した。不登校経験があるタレントの中川翔子さんらが審査委員を務め、公募で募った不登校当事者やその家族計125人もオンラインで審査に参加した。
最優秀賞のcocoさんは「居場所は自分の気持ちによって変化する」というメッセージを動画に込めた。小学6年で不登校になり、オンラインのフリースクールに通った。やっと見つけた居場所だと思ったが、だんだん自分のやりたいことに合わなくなり満足できなくなっていったのがつらかったという。
そんなとき、母の「その時の気持ちに合わせて居場所は変えていくものだ」という言葉に後押しされフリースクールをやめる決断をした。現在は高校受験を目指して努力している。「学校だけが自分の居場所だと思わないでほしい。自分のやりたいことができる環境こそが自分の居場所で、行きたいところに行ってほしい」と語った。
中川さんは「居場所は場所だけではなく、信頼できる人や、趣味、未来などいろんなものであってよいということを動画が教えてくれた。10代だからこそ伝えられる力のこもった言葉を動画で見つけることができる」と話した。
受賞した作品はTikTokで「＃不登校生動画甲子園」と検索すると視聴できる。【萩原桂菜】

title: Emissioni auto, perché le elettriche migliorano la salute dei bambini nelle grandi città
content:
Uno studio di The Lancet dimostra come il calo dei gas di scarico favorisca il recupero della funzionalità polmonare nei più piccoli, confermando i benefici della mobilità a zero emissioni
Zona a basse emissioni, l’esempio di Londra
Ridurre l’inquinamento delle città abbassando le emissioni climalteranti e nocive delle auto a combustione interna, fa bene alla salute dei bambini. Ovviamente non solo a loro ma anche a tutti gli abitanti delle metropoli urbani, ma uno studio scientifico pubblicato su The Lancet Public Health, che ha per protagonista il centro di Londra, ci fornisce una certezza in più.
Nella capitale inglese è stata creata una zona a basse emissioni, chiamata ULEZ, acronimo di Ultra Low Emission Zone, la più grande area urbana al mondo per testare sul campo l’impatto dell’inquinamento prodotto dai veicoli sulla salute dei più piccoli fino ai 9 anni anni. In seguito allo studio quinquennale dal titolo Children’s Health in London and Luton, infatti, sono stati analizzati i miglioramenti della qualità dell’aria.
Meglio Londra o Luton?
I risultati degli studi (condotti da ricercatori della Queen Mary University di Londra) ci dicono che il miglioramento della qualità dell’aria ha contribuito a ripristinare la crescita polmonare precedentemente compromessa dall’esposizione all’inquinamento atmosferico. Gli accademici hanno “selezionato” 3.400 bambini delle scuole elementari, provenienti da 84 istituti londinesi e della cittadina di Luton, usata come sito di controllo per via di una simile combinazione di inquinanti del traffico, ma priva di zona a basse emissioni.
Come si è svolta la ricerca
Mentre nel 2019 è iniziata l’attività di filtro della ULEZ fino a coprire tutta l’area nel 2023, dal 2018 al 2022, durante le visite scolastiche annuali, sono state misurate e monitorate le dimensioni e la salute dei polmoni dei bambini al fine di valutare l’impatto dei cambiamenti nella qualità dell’aria sul loro sviluppo polmonare.
Analizzando i dati raccolti nell’arco di 5 anni, il team ha scoperto che, dopo l’implementazione della ULEZ le dimensioni e la salute dei polmoni dei bambini londinesi sono migliorate rapidamente, raggiungendo livelli paragonabili a quelli dei bambini di Luton. Ancora più importante, hanno dimostrato che questi miglioramenti nella crescita polmonare erano strettamente correlati al miglioramento della qualità dell’aria successiva all’implementazione della ULEZ. Questa barriera urbana che obbliga al pagamento di 12,50 sterline al giorno per circolare nella zona ha avuto conseguenze ben tangibili avendo ridotto il traffico veicolare, soprattutto auto più vecchie, quindi poco efficienti.
Cosa dimostra lo studio
Il team ha valutato la salute e lo sviluppo polmonare dei bambini misurando con precisione il loro volume espiratorio forzato in un secondo, ovvero la quantità di aria che può essere espirata forzatamente dai polmoni dopo un’inspirazione massimale, in relazione all’esposizione al biossido di azoto, l’inquinante più rappresentativo dell’inquinamento da gas di scarico.
I ricercatori hanno scoperto che nei cinque anni successivi all’introduzione della ULEZ, l’esposizione dei bambini londinesi al biossido di azoto è diminuita due volte più velocemente e in misura più che doppia rispetto a quella dei bambini di Luton. Hanno quindi dimostrato che, al diminuire dell’esposizione al biossido di azoto, il volume espiatorio dei piccoli londinesi aumentava di 10 ml all’anno in più rispetto ai bambini di Luton. Al termine dei cinque anni il valore era lo stesso per i bambini di Londra e Luton, indicando che la crescita polmonare dei bambini londinesi si era accelerata durante i cinque anni per “recuperare” il divario con il gruppo di controllo di Luton.
Nel corso dello studio, il team ha osservato che la percentuale di bambini con funzionalità polmonare clinicamente compromessa è diminuita dal 14% al 9% a Londra, rispetto a una diminuzione dal 9% al 7% a Luton. Infatti, il mancato raggiungimento del pieno sviluppo polmonare entro la prima età adulta aumenta il rischio che i bambini sviluppino malattie respiratorie, malattie cardiovascolari e metaboliche e morte prematura in età adulta. Questi risultati, che dimostrano come i deficit nella crescita e nella salute polmonare dei bambini possano essere corretti, hanno pertanto importanti implicazioni per il miglioramento della salute a lungo termine dei bambini.
Il professor Chris Griffiths, docente di medicina generale presso l’Università di Oxford e la Queen Mary University di Londra, coautore senior dello studio, ha dichiarato: “L’inquinamento atmosferico causato dal traffico nelle città danneggia la salute e lo sviluppo dei bambini. Forniamo le prove più solide finora disponibili su come prevenire questi danni. L’istituzione di zone a basse emissioni, con obiettivi ambiziosi, dovrebbe essere considerata una priorità per le città di tutto il mondo che soffrono di inquinamento atmosferico legato al traffico“.
Auto elettriche fanno bene alla salute
Insomma, forzando il concetto, ma neanche troppo in verità, possiamo considerare che l’auto elettrica sarebbe un toccasana per la salute della popolazione giovane e adulta perché sarebbe il contributo più importante nelle affollate metropoli europee ed italiane, alla riduzione di emissioni nocive per la salute umana e dell’ambiente. Infatti, ulteriori dati evidenziano che con l’estensione del traffico limitato la riduzione di NO2 raggiunge il 54%, contro il 27% dello scenario senza l’estensione della ULEZ.
Sebbene la ricerca inglese non si focalizzi unicamente sui veicoli elettrici, è proprio in questo contesto che l’elettrico mostra i suoi punti di forza principali. Ma non è ancora tutto. Non bisogna sottovalutare l’inquinamento acustico ridotto, perché la silenziosità del motore è particolarmente apprezzabile alle basse velocità del traffico cittadino. Ed il fatto che la frenata rigenerativa limita l’uso dei freni tradizionali, riducendo le polveri sottili generate dal consumo delle pastiglie.

title: First River Otter Spotted in the Bronx in 100 Years Along the Bronx River
content:
It was June 23rd when a furry brown arrow shot past a motion-activated camera along the Bronx River and sent conservationists mad with excitement.
It was the first time in approximately 100 years that an otter was observed in this borough of New York City, and provided compelling evidence that decades of conservation and restoration are transforming one of the Big Apple’s most iconic waterways.
The camera was deployed by local scientist RJ Hawkins and overseen by the Wildlife Conservation Society’s (WCS) Education Department, based at the Bronx Zoo.
Hawkins, a graduate of the Miami University of Ohio Advanced Inquiry Program (AIP) hosted at the Bronx Zoo, captured the image while conducting long-term camera trap monitoring for wildlife along the river in concert with the WCS
“When I first reviewed the images, I could hardly believe what I was seeing,” said Hawkins in a statement. “Knowing this may be the first documented river otter in the Bronx in generations was an incredible moment. It shows why long-term wildlife monitoring and environmental restoration efforts matter.”
Craig Piper, WCS’ Interim Executive Vice President of Zoos & Aquarium, and Director of the Bronx Zoo, agreed.
“There are moments in conservation that remind us why this work matters, and this is one of them,” said Piper. “Thanks to a broad coalition of public and private partners, we can celebrate the return of an otter as a result of decades of restoration work to provide cleaner water and healthier habitat. It’s a win for both wildlife and people.”
River otters once ranged throughout New York’s waterways but disappeared from many areas because of pollution, habitat degradation, and unregulated trapping. Today they are considered indicators of healthy freshwater ecosystems because they depend on clean water, abundant fish, and intact river habitats.

The sighting is the latest chapter in the Bronx River’s extraordinary ecological recovery. Once heavily polluted and long regarded as one of the nation’s most neglected urban rivers, the Bronx River has experienced decades of restoration led by public agencies, nonprofit organizations, community volunteers, and conservation partners.
In 2007, beavers returned to the river for the first time in more than 200 years. The appearance of a river otter suggests the river continues to become more hospitable for native wildlife.

While researchers caution that a single observation does not necessarily indicate a resident population, the discovery demonstrates that the Bronx River is increasingly capable of supporting native wildlife that has been absent for generations.
“This otter’s return is a gift, not just to the Bronx River but to the communities that have fought for 50 years to bring this river back to life,” said Javier Lopez with the Bronx River Alliance. “Today, this otter reminds us that when we invest in nature, nature responds, and when communities lead, change is possible.”

title: Google is giving Nigerian students a year of free AI access
content:
Google is giving students at accredited Nigerian universities, polytechnics and colleges of education 12 months of its AI Plus plan for free, bringing its premium AI tools to a generation increasingly using them for schoolwork.
Google said the subscription, worth ₦92,400 ($68.56), gives students access to Gemini Study Notebooks, Gemini Live, Deep Research, interactive 3D visualisations and Google Lens Homework Helper, among other AI-powered learning tools.
The offer is Google’s latest effort to bring its AI tools into education in Africa. In October 2025, the tech giant offered university students in Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, Rwanda, South Africa and Zimbabwe 12 months of free access to Google AI Pro, giving them access to its premium AI tools for research, creativity and learning.
In November, it committed $2.1 million through its philanthropic arm, Google.org, to five Nigerian organisations to accelerate advanced AI skilling and push innovation. The project aimed to support at least 10 higher institutions, train 50 lecturers, 50 teaching assistants, and reach over 11,000 students in two to three years.
“AI is the defining technological shift of our generation, and for Nigeria, with one of the youngest and most entrepreneurial populations in the world, it is an immediate leapfrog opportunity,” said Olumide Balogun, director, West & East Africa at Google. “By offering 12 months of free Google AI Plus for the second consecutive year, we are removing financial barriers so that Nigerian students can master complex subjects, build in-demand digital skills, and compete confidently in the global economy.”
To qualify for the offer, eligible students must verify their enrolment through SheerID, a data platform. Students who claimed the offer last academic year can renew it for another 12 months by verifying their student status again, according to Google.
Once activated, Google AI Plus gives students higher usage limits on Gemini and access to more advanced AI features. They can use Gemini Live for real-time voice conversations, Deep Research to work through long-form research, and custom practice quizzes to study for exams. Students also get unlimited file uploads, alongside 400 gigabytes (GB) of Google storage.
Google noted that its Guided Learning feature is designed to help students understand a topic rather than simply giving them an answer. Google DeepMind tested the approach in June with 1,763 students in West Africa in an eight-week study. According to the study, students who used Guided Learning recorded learning gains equivalent to 1.2 to 1.7 years of typical progress.
According to Google, Nigeria is one of 27 countries in Sub-Saharan Africa where the student offer is now available.
